summary: Reject base continuations whose retained numeric research effects are all zero.
details: Normalization rejects all-zero modifiers or recipe-productivity changes through the shared integrity helper, with a failed effect gate and zero_base_extension_effects reason. Planned ownership uses the same helper when removal leaves only zero values, preserving its existing rejection and ledger.

Consumed compiler controls reject all-zero continuations before and after planned ownership and preserve mixed effects. Controlled finalizer checks exercise four adapters, recipe-change semantics, signed and small values, existing nonnumeric forms and previous empty/ownership regressions.

The existing ownership facts module now owns the duplicated material-stage pair predicate used by resolution and compilation validation. Parent identities, effect signatures and the exactly-two-claims rule remain required; the existing module size limits are retained.

The selected ownership architecture check now enforces canonical shared bytes across its four current target scopes. Its historical receipt, target proofs and module size limits remain separate and unchanged; source binding checks do not claim actual package or native qualification.

This is an exact-zero admission check, not native usefulness or saturation proof. Actual package rewards, native ownership interactions, upgrades, multiplayer and performance still require qualification; save and migration acceptance remain open.
